candidate.answerReason: The shaded area is the area of a rectangle of dimensions \(4\sqrt{2}\) by \(2\), less two triangles of area \(2\) each and two sectors of area \(\pi/2\) each.

methods.label: Subtract triangles and sectors from a rectangle
methods.explanation:
Enclose the shaded region in rectangle \(ABFE\). Its unshaded parts can be separated into triangles and sectors.

[Figure 1](figures/2007_AMC_10A_Q24_question_fig1.svg)

A radius to a tangency point is perpendicular to the tangent. Thus \(AE\) and \(BF\) are perpendicular to \(EF\). They both have length \(2\), and the centers lie on the same side of \(EF\), so \(ABFE\) is a rectangle. Since \(O\) is the midpoint of \(AB\), its dimensions are
\[
AB=2AO=4\sqrt{2},\qquad AE=2.
\]
To find the missing pieces, draw radii \(AC\) and \(BD\). Because \(OC\) is tangent, \(AC\perp OC\). The Pythagorean theorem gives
\[
OC^2=AO^2-AC^2=(2\sqrt{2})^2-2^2=4,
\]
so \(OC=2=AC\). Therefore \(\triangle AOC\) is right isosceles, with \(\angle CAO=45^\circ\). Since \(\angle EAO=90^\circ\), the sector angle \(\angle EAC\) is \(45^\circ\). The same reasoning on the right gives \(OD=BD=2\) and \(\angle FBD=45^\circ\).

The rectangle consists of the shaded region, triangles \(AOC\) and \(BOD\), and sectors \(EAC\) and \(FBD\), with disjoint interiors. Each triangle has area \(\tfrac12\cdot2\cdot2=2\), and each sector has area
\[
\frac{45}{360}\pi(2)^2=\frac{\pi}{2}.
\]
Consequently, the shaded area is
\[
(4\sqrt{2})(2)-2(2)-2\left(\frac{\pi}{2}\right)
=\boxed{8\sqrt{2}-4-\pi},
\]
which is choice \(\boxed{\text{B}}\).
